clue.text: Suffer at home — cut up rough only initially

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the three words before it is wanted

explanation.surface: A householder endures domestic trouble that turns nasty only at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on yourself and undergo it.

clue.text: Mostly fashionable groups left

parts.note: something in fashion is in
genera are groups in biological classification

explanation.surface: Most of the trendy cliques have departed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or on the whole, as a broad rule.

clue.text: Conservative and socialist are divided

parts.note: socialists belong to the political left

explanation.surface: Tory and Labour politicians cannot agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft means split apart, as in a cleft chin or rock.

clue.text: Engineer, exhausted, went to bed

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
exhausted means tired

explanation.surface: A worn-out mechanic turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is to go off to sleep.

clue.text: Archbishop — a bishop perhaps following the trade of Simon Peter

definitions.text: following the trade of Simon Peter

parts.note: Geoffrey Fisher was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1945 to 1961
a bishop is one of the chessmen, so an example of a man

explanation.surface: A church leader is said to share the apostle Peter's line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person who follows Simon Peter's trade: Peter fished on the Sea of Galilee before joining Jesus. Geoffrey Fisher crowned Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter caught fish for a living, so one following his trade works with nets and boats.

clue.text: Reverse providing a second business failure

indicators.note: Reverse tells us the word for providing is turned backwards

parts.note: providing means if, as a condition
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A setback causes a second firm to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete fiasco is a humiliating flop or disaster.

clue.text: Outline provided by poet in English? On the contrary

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
On the contrary flips the stated order, so English goes inside the poet rather than the poet inside English

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet

explanation.surface: A draft framework is supplied by a poet writing in English.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue puts the poet inside English; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so E goes inside SKELTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton draft or plan is a bare framework, the basic structure.

clue.text: Note — catching fish is my mission

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: catching means the word my surrounds and traps the fish

parts.note: taken as written
a bass is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler explains that hooking fish is their purpose in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission is an embassy, the office of an ambassador abroad.

clue.text: Diagrams beginning to reveal incorrect timing of carnival

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters are set down wrongly, so rearranged
beginning to picks only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Charts showing wrongly when a festival takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the day itself: Shrove Tuesday, the climax of the carnival season.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, the feast day that closes carnival season before Lent.

clue.text: What joggers do, for instance, with a horse coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example
a dun is a horse of dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Runners pass, for example, beside a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joggers' look like runners, but they are people who jog someone, giving a prod.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give them a light prod with the elbow.

clue.text: A big creature with short hair Hans Christian Andersen?

definitions.text: A big creature with short hair

explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a huge smooth-coated dog; Andersen, famed Copenhagen storyteller, was an eminent man of Denmark.

clue.text: "Not interested", the directors say

indicators.note: say tells us the word for the directors is heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: The company's board brush off a proposal as uninteresting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weary and lacking any curiosity is fed up and uninterested.

clue.text: Tuckets recur in a dance composition

indicators.note: dance as a command tells these letters to jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: Trumpet fanfares come round again within a ballet score.
explanation.walkthrough: A tucket is an old word for a trumpet flourish; 'dance' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet suite is a musical work, a piece written by a composer.

clue.text: Some brassieres I decline to hang out

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to peg certain bras on the washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out somewhere, in slang, is to live or dwell there.

clue.text: Sally holds the stage, predicting the future

indicators.note: holds means the word for sally contains the stage

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden attack out of a besieged place
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An actress called Sally dominates the theatre with prophecies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by drawing lots, a form of fortune-telling.

clue.text: The Scriptures worthily translated

indicators.note: translated suggests these letters are rendered into another form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The Bible rendered into another language with due reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is a set phrase for the sacred texts of the Bible.

clue.text: Place great value on the right official

parts.note: to treasure something is to prize it highly
R is short for right

explanation.surface: Esteem the proper functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who handles a club's or society's finances.

clue.text: Wise man's investment in spirits needs thorough searches

indicators.note: investment in means clothing, the word for spirits being wrapped round the wise man

parts.note: rums are spirits distilled from sugar cane
a mage is a magus or wise man

explanation.surface: A magus putting money into liquor needs to look carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummages are hunts through things in an untidy, thorough way.

clue.text: Bird approaches branch a bloomer

indicators.note: approaches puts the bird up against the branch, coming just before it

parts.note: a lark is a songbird
a spur is an offshoot, as of a railway line or mountain range

explanation.surface: A songbird flies in towards a tree limb with a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' reads as a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium-like flowering plant: a bloomer is anything that bears flowers.

clue.text: Inadequate entrance of Shakespeare's Shylock

indicators.note: entrance of picks the opening letter, the way into the word

parts.note: Shylock is the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: Shylock makes a weak first appearance on the Shakespearean stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender resources or chances are slight, too small to be enough.

clue.text: Henry, in class, is virtuous

indicators.note: in places the letter for Henry inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A boy named Henry is well behaved at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and morally upright, especially sexually.

clue.text: Noisome noise made by singer

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a stinking place hums, so it is smelly; and crooning with closed lips is a soft sung sound.

clue.text: Way crosses the river and follows the coast

indicators.note: crosses puts the river right after the way, as if passing over it
follows puts the word and after the river

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
R is short for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road bridges a stream and then hugs the shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a beach or shore, the land at the water's edge.

clue.text: Miss the brim very un-characteristically curse

indicators.note: acting out of character means these letters behave unusually, so are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman unusually misses a hat's brim and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a stage pirate's mock oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional comic sailor's oath, an exclamation of surprise or annoyance.

clue.text: Smollett turned up without one shoe

indicators.note: without says a letter is left out
turned up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The novelist appeared missing a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes SAIBOT; 'without one' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a type of footwear.

clue.text: East with an honour used wastefully

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here A
in bridge the ten is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: East holding a top card plays it carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: East is a seat at the bridge table, which sets up the card sense of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed is gone, used up rather than kept.

clue.text: Money in a …

parts.note: slang for cash, and also what a roll is made of; the clue runs on into the next clue's word roll

explanation.surface: Cash rolled up in a wad.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 25-across: 'Money in a ... roll'. The word 'roll' belongs to both clues; here it means a bread roll, and the slang sense is cash.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, dough or loot means cash, and a baker's roll is made of the same stuff.

clue.text: roll returned-pleased one leading fighter

indicators.note: leading puts these pieces in front of the next part

parts.note: pleased means glad
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: returned says the word for roll is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a delighted person heads into battle with a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ROTA into ATOR; the first word 'roll' continues 24-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant trained to battle others or wild beasts for public entertainment.

clue.text: Supposed other side to be organised

indicators.note: to be organised means these letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A team's opponents need to be well drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorised means proposed as a hypothesis, put forward as an idea.

clue.text: One lost the King protecting the ace

indicators.note: protecting means the letters for the King surround and shield the others

parts.note: GR is George Rex, King George
an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: A card player is beaten even though the king guards the ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A person past saving or doomed is beyond hope, finished.
